Figure_20_Molecular_vector_fields.caption: Figure 20. Vector fields and rotational curvature of the constrained molecular family. A,B, The two mass-horizontal velocity fields at isomer A’s base conformation, displayed on its experimental-identity-linked generated heavy-atom geometry. Arrows show 1.2 rad times the instantaneous all-atom horizontal velocity, restricted to the displayed heavy atoms; they are tangent vectors, not finite displacements. The mass projection includes explicit hydrogens. Atom positions and the camera are fixed between panels. C, Norm of the body-section connection curvature on a 25-by25 periodic grid. Its angular-coordinate convention is fixed; individual body components are archived. D, The square-loop reconstruction error compared with the predicted negative curvature vector, decreasing with loop size for both independently generated case slices. The scaled error is the norm of log(R)/epsilon squared plus F12, with the rotation log identified with its axial vector. The loop starts along positive q1 then positive q2. The fields remove overall angular momentum, and their nonzero vertical Lie bracket explains rotational holonomy. No receptor mechanism or experimental trajectory is inferred.

Figure_21_Reduced_Hamiltonian_motion.caption: Figure 21. Reduced Hamiltonian motion on the same fixed molecular slices. A, The two angle coordinates from zero initial angles and a positive q1 velocity normalized to 0.5 kcal/mol kinetic energy. B, Kinetic and restricted MMFF94s potential energy for isomer A; their sum remains 0.5 kcal/mol to the recorded numerical precision. C, Proper-rotation angle reconstructed at zero angular momentum. Time conversion uses 48.8882 fs per declared natural unit. D, An additional validation after the primary trajectories: fixed-step RK4 solves the forced geodesic equation in angles and velocities, independently organized from the canonical DOP853 momentum integration. Endpoint errors decrease at approximately fourth order under step halving; the dotted line indicates slope only. No physical parameter or endpoint was retuned. These are deterministic constrained-model paths without solvent, thermostat or a receptor, and are not full molecular dynamics or measured motions.

Figure_22_Quantum_rotor_analysis.caption: Figure 22. Effective quantum torsional model with approximation limits retained. A, Ground-state Ritz values for both cases at three coefficient-grid sizes and six nested Fourier cutoffs. Each fixed-grid sequence decreases variationally; differences at the largest cutoff remain material. B, Complete finite-basis partition sums at 298.15 K and N = 129 increase with nested basis size, as the fixed-operator convergence theorem requires. C,D, N = 129,K = 15 quantum minus classical position-density quadratures, multiplied by 129 squared so the plotted density is relative to uniform angle measure. Blue is negative and orange positive on one symmetric scale. The underlying coefficient model uses exact Fourier integrals of periodic bilinear rho, rho g-inverse and rho E interpolants. These densities are not claimed converged quantum corrections or ab initio populations. An exact reflected model is isospectral; the two independently generated case slices need not be. Matrix residuals and spectral-weight truncation checks concern the finite model and do not certify excluded modes or physical accuracy.

Figure_23_Protein_closure_topology.caption: Figure 23. Experimental protein backbones and closure-dependent knot evidence. A-C, First-model chain-A C-alpha traces of 1J85 (YibK), 2EFV (MJ0366), and 1UBQ (ubiquitin). Tube colour progresses from N to C along each independent chain; endpoint beads are blue and orange. The physical 10 Å scale bars use the stored orthographic cameras; the proteins are not shown at a common magnification. D, Exact Fox cofactor determinants after 64 far-point closures in fixed Fibonacci-sphere directions. Counts are 57/4/2/1 for determinants 3/5/1/9 in 1J85, 50/14 for 3/1 in 2EFV, and 63/1 for 1/3 in 1UBQ. Every closure is retained. Determinant 1 does not prove an unknot, determinant 3 does not uniquely prove a trefoil, and the determinant cannot distinguish mirror handedness. Three independent new projections of each closed polygon give 576 additional matching determinant checks. These frequencies describe the closure protocol and are not random-sampling probabilities or biological-function estimates.

Figure_24_Quantum_braid_invariants.caption: Figure 24. Genuine quantum-topological algebra, distinguished from the quantum rotor. A,B, A mathematical closed trefoil polygon and its exact mirror, with the same camera. This is not a protein coordinate model. C, The algebraic crossing convention is fixed independently of a visual handedness label. The positive two-strand braid convention gives V(t)=t+t^3-t^4; reflection inverts t, giving different Laurent coefficients. These exact polynomials obstruct knot achirality but are not complete invariants. D, A two-dimensional Temperley-Lieb representation at t=exp(2pi i/5) obeys unitarity and the braid relation to floating precision while the two generators do not commute. The exact diagram state sum separately checks braid relations and both Markov stabilization signs. The ordinary trace of these 2-by2 matrices is not the Jones closure trace. No quantum algorithm or molecular braid operation was executed. Reflection-even Hamiltonian spectra can remain identical between mirror sectors even when the Jones coefficients differ.
